articles.title: Microsoft restores Outlook and Teams after global outage that may have cost businesses $7 billion
articles.excerpt: Microsoft said early Saturday it had fixed the network fault that cut off Outlook, Teams and Copilot for more than 24 hours across more than 70 countries, as one think tank put lost productivity near $7 billion.
articles.author: fiveboroughbulletin-staff
articles.imageCaption: Microsoft's headquarters campus in Redmond, Washington
articles.imageAlt: Microsoft's headquarters campus in Redmond, Washington
content: Microsoft said early Saturday that it had finished repairing the fault behind a global outage that cut off Outlook, Teams and its Copilot assistant for more than 24 hours, restoring service to the last affected customers and regions, [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/microsoft-battling-major-outage/) and the Associated Press reported. The disruption began shortly before 1 p.m. ET on Thursday, [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/US/outlook-down-microsoft-outage-reported-mail/story?id=138088203) reported, and reached users in more than 70 countries and territories, according to Downdetector. The [Australian Associated Press](https://www.crookwellgazette.com.au/story/9391504/microsoft-services-fully-recover-after-global-outage/) described it as one of the longest outages in Microsoft's history.

Microsoft said the failure was a technical problem rather than a cyberattack, and that artificial intelligence agents played no role. The company traced it to a flaw introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a more recent network change, [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/US/outlook-down-microsoft-outage-reported-mail/story?id=138088203) reported. Engineers paused deployments, moved traffic off the affected infrastructure and restarted servers, and [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/microsoft-outage-outlook-aws-google.html) reported that some servers were failing automated health checks. Early Friday, Microsoft reported positive results for server stability after patching an upstream authentication and routing configuration component on part of its infrastructure, [NBC News](https://nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/live-blog/microsoft-outage-outlook-teams-updates-fix-rcna609118) reported. Charles Lamanna, the executive who oversees Copilot, agents and the platform, said technical challenges made the recovery harder than normal and promised a post-mortem with a step-by-step timeline and repair items, according to CBS News.

The reach was wide. Downdetector logged more than 130,000 user reports on Thursday alone, CBS News said, and more than 7.4 million worldwide over the whole incident, peaking at nearly 20,000 a minute, according to the Australian Associated Press. Microsoft says more than 430 million people use its 365 apps, CBS News noted, though it is unclear how many were affected. New York City's emergency management agency warned residents of delays reaching city agencies, ABC News reported, and CBS News and the Associated Press reported that Singapore's government technology agency said official email was down, Japan's government said its IT infrastructure was affected, and the Philippine Supreme Court reported disruptions. Workhorse Group delayed a quarterly earnings call because of the outage, and OpenAI and Anthropic each reported problems connecting to Microsoft 365 tools, according to the same report. The outage also delayed trading firms and kept some companies from publishing earnings, the Australian Associated Press said.

Estimates of the cost are already in the billions. Anderson Economic Group, a Michigan think tank, put the lost productivity at about $7 billion, [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/12/tech/microsoft-outage-cripples-office-workers-nationwide) reported, with its president, Patrick Anderson, saying as many as 26 million users on Thursday and 51 million on Friday suffered a real economic loss. CNN's [live coverage](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/12/business/live-news/microsoft-global-outage-intl-hnk) added that the firm is known for cautious estimates, that many affected users likely faced only annoyance, and that customer refund claims could push the total above $7 billion. The hit to insurers looks far smaller: Mario De Cicco of Morningstar DBRS put global insured losses at $300 million to $500 million, below the $400 million to $1.5 billion toll of the 2024 CrowdStrike outage, the Australian Associated Press reported. In Australia, an RSM risk adviser said professional-services firms could lose hundreds of thousands of dollars an hour, [ABC News Australia](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-13/microsoft-outlook-outage-cost-to-businesses/107381570) reported.

Investors largely looked past it. Microsoft shares were down about 3 percent in premarket trading Friday, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) reported, but recovered during the session and closed flat at $523.88, the Australian Associated Press said. The stock is up roughly 8 percent this year. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. said the episode raises major questions for the company, CBS News reported. The longer-term worry is reliability: eToro analyst Josh Gilbert said a recurring problem would give IT departments a reason to think twice about putting more business with one provider, while other analysts noted that steep switching costs make defections unlikely, according to the Australian Associated Press. The wire report noted that Microsoft 365 also suffered outages in January this year and last October, and that its Azure cloud platform had one last month.

Microsoft has apologized and said it takes the trust of its customers seriously. Australia's home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said Microsoft likened the incident to the 2024 CrowdStrike outage, where a faulty update went awry, CBS News and the Associated Press reported. Ookla analyst Luke Kehoe said the episode shows how much of the working day runs through one provider's email and collaboration tools, according to the Australian Associated Press. As of early Saturday, Microsoft had not yet published its promised post-mortem.

articles.title: Nvidia hires former federal prosecutor to lead Huang probe as shares slide for a second day
articles.excerpt: The board retained Wachtell Lipton and ex-U.S. attorney Joon Kim to run the inquiry as the stock fell again Tuesday, with the FBI, Congress and shareholder litigation now circling the AI bellwether.
articles.author: fiveboroughbulletin-staff
articles.imageCaption: Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California
articles.imageAlt: Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California
content: Nvidia's independent directors have retained the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and former acting U.S. attorney Joon H. Kim to lead an investigation of chief executive Jensen Huang, the company said Tuesday, as the chipmaker's shares fell for a second straight session. The board described the work as a "thorough and independent" inquiry, [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/nvidia-board-jensen-huang-inquiry-directors-succession) reported, and said it is the same review it announced on Sunday.

The board opened the inquiry after reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. U.S. intelligence agencies concluded that Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, was passing information to Beijing, according to reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times that [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/nvidia-jensen-huang-chinese-spy-investigation.html) summarized. The two are not related. Huang told employees in an email that he had been unfaithful to his wife, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/nvidia-nvda-jensen-huang-affair-chinese-spy.html) reported, without giving details. China's Foreign Ministry has dismissed the spying claims as a smear, [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/9/nvidia-shares-slump-amid-investigation-into-ceo-jensen-huang) reported, and Nvidia has said its board has no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised.

Investors have punished the stock. Nvidia fell 4.3 percent on Monday to close at $178.67, the [Associated Press](https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/nvidia-shares-jensen-huang-investigation/4172764/) reported, and slid roughly 5.5 percent more on Tuesday, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/nvidia-nvda-jensen-huang-affair-chinese-spy.html). Its market value briefly dipped below $4 trillion in afternoon trading before recovering to close above that mark. The shares were already down about 23 percent over the previous 30 days as worries about an AI-sector bubble weighed on the group, and they hit an all-time high only last month.

Analysts have mostly argued that Huang is unlikely to be forced out, while acknowledging the uncertainty. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. put the odds of his removal at roughly 15 percent and said a board investigation could take four to six weeks, leaving an overhang on the stock until more news emerges, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/nvidia-nvda-jensen-huang-affair-chinese-spy.html) reported. Huang is Nvidia's fifth-largest shareholder with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to LSEG data cited by [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/9/nvidia-shares-slump-amid-investigation-into-ceo-jensen-huang), but unlike the founders of some other major technology companies he does not hold majority voting control.

The story widened on Tuesday. The Information reported that Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, which it said dated to 2023, helped facilitate shipments of at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips to Chinese companies through a network of firms she built with her husband and sister, [Reuters](https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/nvidia-ceos-affair-aided-7-5-billion-chip-shipments-china/) reported, citing two people who know her. [24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/10/nivida-chinese-spy-story-is-getting-worse-huangs-affair-helped-move-7-5-billion-in-chips-to-china/) noted that Reuters could not independently verify the claim, and Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Separately, a Reuters review of shipping records found that Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary imported Nvidia hardware, including H100 processors, between 2024 and 2026, though shipments into Indonesia do not by themselves show that the chips were diverted to China or that export rules were broken, [Indian Television](https://indiantelevision.com/technology/from-an-affair-to-an-ai-security-crisis-why-jensen-huangs-personal-life-is-now-nvidias-problem/) summarized.

Washington has become directly involved. President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI was looking into the matter while saying he believed Huang had no idea the woman was a spy, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nvidias-outofhour-shares-fall-as-firm-probes-ceo-jensen-huang-5010476) and [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trump-nvidia-jensen-huang-republican-congress-leaders-morning-rundown-rcna608496) reported, and an NBC source said the Justice Department's separate criminal investigation of Megaspeed also examines whether the company smuggled Nvidia chips into China. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer called for a full accounting of Trump's defense of Huang and urged lawmakers to quickly approve new restrictions on U.S. chip exports, [The Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-nvidia-stock-market-value-ceo-jensen-huang-affair-fallout/) reported. A proposed shareholder class action filed Monday in federal court in San Jose accuses Nvidia and Huang of misleading investors about the relationship and the company's dealings with Megaspeed, according to CNBC.

The next test comes quickly. Nvidia is scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter results on November 17, [The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/10/prediction-nov-17-will-be-a-huge-day-for-the-stock-market/) noted, its first report since the [record $96.2 billion quarter](/business/nvidia-posts-record-quarterly-revenue) it posted in August. Three House Republican committee chairs have also asked Huang to meet privately with lawmakers later this month, [Quartz](https://qz.com/nvidia-stock-board-investigation-jensen-huang-spy-110926) reported, and the board has said it has confidence in Huang and his leadership team.

articles.title: Lakers sale to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger values team at record $12.5 billion
articles.excerpt: The agreement marks the largest valuation ever placed on a North American sports franchise and hands control to two of the buyers who lost out on the team a year earlier.
articles.author: fiveboroughbulletin-staff
content: The Los Angeles Lakers are being sold in a deal that values the franchise at a record $12.5 billion, according to terms confirmed this week, marking the highest price ever placed on a professional sports team in North America.

The buying group is led by venture capitalist Josh Kushner, founder of Thrive Capital, alongside Bob Iger, the former longtime chief executive of Disney. The seller is Mark Walter, chief executive of TWG Global and controlling owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers, who had taken control of the Lakers just over a year earlier in a deal that valued the team at roughly $10 billion.

That earlier transaction effectively ended the Buss family's decades-long ownership of the franchise, though Jeanie Buss is expected to remain the team's governor for at least five years under continuity terms attached to the sale, preserving her public role in overseeing basketball operations.

The new deal still requires approval from the NBA's Board of Governors, a process that typically takes several weeks as the league reviews buyer financing and ownership structure. Neither the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks nor the Dodgers are included in the transaction, which is limited to the Lakers franchise itself.

The jump in valuation over such a short period underscores how aggressively sports franchise prices have climbed in recent years, driven by lucrative media rights deals, rising interest from private equity and wealthy individual investors, and the scarcity of marquee teams that ever come up for sale. Sports business analysts said the price also reflects the Lakers' particular standing as one of the most recognizable brands in global sports.

Kushner and Iger have not detailed plans for the franchise's day-to-day operations, though people familiar with the deal said continuity in the front office and coaching staff is expected in the near term as the ownership transition is finalized.

articles.title: Nvidia posts record $96.2 billion quarter as data center demand keeps climbing
articles.excerpt: Revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, extending the chipmaker's streak of beating Wall Street expectations to fifteen straight quarters.
articles.author: fiveboroughbulletin-staff
content: Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $96.2 billion for the three months ended in late July, a 106 percent jump from the same period a year earlier, as demand for the chips underpinning artificial intelligence systems continued to outpace even the company's own aggressive production plans.

The data center segment, which sells the processors used to train and run large AI models, accounted for the bulk of that growth, with revenue in the division rising 117 percent year over year to $89 billion. Overall revenue also climbed 18 percent from the prior quarter, a pace few companies of Nvidia's size have managed to sustain for this long.

Profitability held up alongside the revenue growth, with the company reporting a gross margin of 75 percent. Chief executive Jensen Huang described the current period of AI infrastructure buildout as reaching a new stage in which the computing capacity being deployed is now generating meaningful revenue for the customers buying it, rather than remaining a purely speculative expense.

It was the fifteenth consecutive quarter in which Nvidia's results topped Wall Street analysts' consensus estimates, a run that has made its earnings report one of the most closely watched events on the corporate calendar for investors trying to gauge the broader health of AI spending.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress told analysts the company expects continued growth into the current quarter, though she cautioned that gross margins are likely to narrow slightly, into the low seventies percentage range, as the cost of memory components used in its newest chips rises.

Shares moved in after-hours trading following the report before settling into a more mixed pattern the next day, as some investors weighed the strong headline numbers against questions about how long the current pace of data center spending by big technology companies can continue.

articles.title: FAA orders crack inspections on hundreds of Boeing 737 MAX jets
articles.excerpt: The directive covers 471 U.S.-registered aircraft after a structural issue previously found on older 737 models turned up in planes sharing the same design.
articles.author: fiveboroughbulletin-staff
content: The Federal Aviation Administration has finalized a directive ordering airlines to inspect 471 U.S.-registered Boeing 737 MAX jets for potential cracking in a structural support near the aircraft's forward service door and galley area, extending a safety issue previously identified on older 737 models to the newer MAX family.

The affected component, known as a bear strap, reinforces the fuselage around the forward entry area. Regulators say cracking had already been confirmed on a number of older 737 NG aircraft that share a similar structural design and assembly process, prompting the FAA to require operators of MAX 8, MAX 9 and 737-8200 variants to check for the same issue even though no cracks have yet been confirmed on those newer jets.

The directive takes effect in mid-September and sets out an inspection schedule tied to how heavily each aircraft has been used, requiring operators to repair any cracking found before returning a plane to passenger service. The FAA said the order does not require any aircraft to be grounded immediately, since the inspection window is designed to catch the issue well before it could become a safety concern.

Boeing said in a statement that it supports the directive and is working with airline customers to complete the inspections on the standard timeline, characterizing the issue as one that its engineering teams identified proactively as part of ongoing structural reviews across the 737 fleet.

The order lands amid a period of heightened regulatory attention on Boeing's manufacturing quality, following several years of scrutiny that intensified after a door plug panel blew out on a 737 MAX 9 during an Alaska Airlines flight in early 2024. Aviation regulators and airlines alike have since adopted a lower threshold for ordering precautionary inspections on the MAX family.

Airlines operating the affected jets, including several of the largest U.S. domestic carriers, said they expect to complete the required checks within routine maintenance schedules without significant disruption to flight operations.

articles.title: Zillow cuts more than 500 jobs as it resets its cost structure
articles.excerpt: The real estate platform's chief executive told staff the cuts were about discipline rather than any single new project or technology.
articles.author: fiveboroughbulletin-staff
content: Zillow is cutting just over 500 jobs, the online real estate company confirmed this week, in a restructuring that chief executive Jeremy Wacksman described to staff as an effort to keep the company's cost base disciplined rather than a response to any single business setback.

In an internal message announcing the cuts, Wacksman said the changes were intended to sharpen focus on the company's core priorities and were not primarily driven by the adoption of artificial intelligence tools, pushing back on a narrative that has accompanied a number of other technology-sector layoffs this year.

The reductions touch multiple divisions of the company, according to people familiar with the plan, and come as the broader housing market has cooled from the frantic pace of previous years, with elevated mortgage rates continuing to weigh on the volume of home sales that platforms like Zillow rely on for advertising and referral revenue.

Affected employees are being offered severance packages and continued benefits for a transition period, the company said, consistent with the terms it has used in prior rounds of job cuts. Zillow has trimmed staff several times since 2022, including a larger restructuring tied to the wind-down of its home-flipping business.

The cuts add to a wider pattern across the real estate and technology sectors this year, as companies balance continued investment in artificial intelligence features against pressure from investors to show tighter cost control. Zillow's stock has been volatile in recent months as investors weigh slower transaction volumes against the company's efforts to expand into rentals, mortgages and other adjacent services.
